title: Patterns
slide_intent: Teach designers to vary a graphic through scale and subdivision while keeping the angles that relate its versions. A viewer can then recognize the family even when the density changes.
strategic_value: CSAIL can extend the geometry of its mark into supporting surfaces. The website header shows how angular forms can frame subject-specific imagery and leave room for the lab identity and a topic title.
demonstration: Two black pattern specimens sit above a laptop mockup. The right specimen divides its shapes into narrower bands. The laptop header crops differently colored images into adjacent angled fields.
practical_value: Compare a broad subdivision with a finer one before choosing the scale of a header pattern. Use the laptop example to check that graphic detail leaves the identifier and title readable.

content_islands.name: Pattern guidance
content_islands.spec: Set the page title and rationale in the narrow left column. Group the notes on source geometry, scale and possible uses.

content_islands.name: Paired specimens
content_islands.spec: Across the top of a pale field, place two black arrangements of polygonal cells. Draw thin light divisions in both and use a denser subdivision at right.

content_islands.name: Website header
content_islands.spec: Center a laptop beneath the specimens. Divide its header imagery with angled edges and retain a separate white band for the identifier and Fintech title.

content_islands.name: Book footer
content_islands.spec: Align the short-guide identifier, laboratory name and folio along the bottom margin.
